title: Pier Maria Rossi di San Secondo to Ferrante Gonzaga, San Secondo, 4 and 8 Nov 1537 (Biblioteca Estense, Campori R cc. 31-34; catalogue 1564, the Rossi letters): read in part

plaintext.source: No decipherment on any leaf of cc. 31-34 (seen on the images).

transcription.notes: Counted by scripts/build.py (units.tsv), not by docs/_check_profile.py --measure, so measured is false. 36 cipher lines: c. 31r L01-L22 (910 units), c. 31v V01-V14 (703 units); a clear close follows on c. 31v. First transcription by one reader, frozen before any decoding; it codes two tall-sign shapes (d and t) as one sign P. documents.route: Pier Maria Rossi, count of San Secondo (San Secondo) to Ferrante Gonzaga, viceroy of Sicily

plaintext.source: No decipherment on any leaf of cc. 31-34 (seen on the images).

transcription.source: Estense Digital Library IIIF images (edl-jarvis.cultura.gov.it), record 4a838739-0cb9-409f-93e5-c1076143ddb3
transcription.notes: Counted by scripts/build.py (units.tsv); measured is false. 17 cipher lines on c. 33r (755 units), then a clear close. Same readers and method as letter A.

system.summary: Simple substitution on a symbol alphabet of 25 signs for 20 letters, with homophones for a, i, c, g and u, no nulls and no code groups seen. Roman numerals and one Latin word are left in clear inside the cipher. Two of the letters, d and t, are tall signs that differ only in the head: a hook closed onto the stem for d, an open hat over a separate tick for t.
system.doubled_letters: written once in most words (the writer's spelling); tt as two ticks under one hat
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the sign codes of the first transcription without the blot mark: 25 with a value, 3 without (A, the apostrophe mark, the bare tick). The first transcription gives the d and t shapes one code, P (256 units), so the transcription as it stands is polyphonic at that sign; the cipher is not. Told apart by shape, a second look that knew the hypothesis and a blind test on crops agree on 178 of 215 P signs (82.8%). In practice d or t is chosen from context. The sign # is a for the small form and q for the tall form before u. Gaps on the sheet often, not always, fall at word ends.

prior_solution.where: None found; priority not established. Checked: this repository (catalogue row 1564 open, no target folder), the leaves themselves (no decipherment), the Estense records, and six web searches of 11 Nov 2026. Not checked: Archivio Gonzaga, Mantua, b. 1911; Archivio di Stato di Parma, Famiglia Rossi bb. 8-12; the Rossi di San Secondo archive (Lincei/Corsiniana) series I cart. 26; the Olschki volumes on the Gonzaga papers; the Guicciardini and Aretino correspondence editions.

conditions.human_role: Malcolm McBratney directed the work, set the rules (every attempt recorded, a transcription frozen before decoding, a blind second transcription, shuffled-key and null controls, a blind shape test, no claim without its check) and sent the result; Claude sessions picked the letters from the catalogue, transcribed, solved, read and checked. No reading by a person without AI.
tools: own Python annealer with Italian quadgrams (homophonic substitution)
shuffled-key baseline, 5,000 keys; frequency-preserving permutation controls
Estense IIIF images: 1,024 px tiles stitched at full resolution, line strips and crops
models: Claude (Anthropic), several sessions of 11-12 Nov 2026 (model ids not recorded)
claude-fable-5-2 (session of 12 Nov 2026 that prepared this folder)

solution.what: First transcription of cc. 31r, 31v and 33r from the IIIF images by one reader, frozen (hashes recorded) before any decoding: 53 lines, 2,368 cipher units, 28 sign codes. It codes the d and t shapes as one sign.
Own annealer tested on a synthetic Italian text of 904 characters with d and t merged and homophones: 86.5% of letters recovered.

Annealer with Italian quadgrams on the frozen transcription, six restarts of 50,000 steps: -4.227 per character and continuous Italian ('che Pinarolo et Turino sono socorsi et dodici pezi de artiglieria'). No crib, no gloss.
Key table completed by reading, the reading aligned unit by unit to the frozen transcription. The sign P read d 89 times and t 152 times: two shapes under one code.

Key-only decryption against 5,000 shuffled keys: whole text -4.319 against a best of -5.713; letter A -4.328 (best -5.745); letter B -4.295 (best -5.561); none of the 5,000 as good. Letter B with a key voted from letter A's reading only: -4.314 against a best of -5.644.
Held-out variants: an annealer key fitted on letter A alone reads 82.4% of letter B's units (it merges rare letters); the same with a letter-frequency penalty reads 62.8% and was dropped.
Blind second transcription of all 53 lines by another session that opened only the page images: 2,247 of 2,363 aligned units agree with the first (95.09%). It did not split d from t either.
Second look at every tall sign read d (89): 79 have the closed hook, 4 the t shape, 6 undecided or leaning. Not blind: the reader knew the hypothesis. Consensus count 2,247 of 2,368 units (94.89%).

The annealer on five frequency-preserving permutations of the cipher stream: all five end at -4.610 per character (a degenerate key), against -4.227 for the real stream. With the letter budget limited: real -4.230, three controls -4.971 to -4.983.

Blind shape test: the 358 tall signs cut out under random ids and classed by a reader who saw only the crops. Against the second look it agrees on 178 of 215 P signs (82.8%). With the blind classes in place of the second look the count is 2,204 of 2,368 units (93.07%).

For this folder: both letters written out in full as sentences with every hole in place, the clear closes read from the image, five unread places looked at again on the image (three new doubtful words, no hole closed).

Six web searches for an edition or decipherment of the letters; the repository and the Estense records. Nothing found. The Mantua and Parma archives and the printed Gonzaga literature were not searched in full text.

Integration check: a decoder written separately reproduces the K lines of decryption_A.txt and decryption_B.txt (53 of 53 lines, A recto and verso, B); blind against non-blind shape verdicts recomputed from dt_ledger.tsv (178 of 215 = 82.8%, as stated); agreement with the reading corrected to 187 of 241 (blind) and 214 of 241 (non-blind) where the contributor's 195 and 231 counted unclear and unseen signs; word counts checked against the readings; stamped-file hashes and RFC 3161 imprints checked; about 70 signs of the first part of V01-V03 compared with the image.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2295 tokens, 26 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.33 per letter; random keys -4.835 (z 4.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.958 (mean -2.966, z 95.3); annealer on the real text -2.323. Verdict: underdetermined.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.147; polyphony 0.058; 73 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.323

outcome.method_basis: An annealer with Italian quadgrams on the frozen first transcription gave continuous Italian without any crib; the leaves carry no decipherment. The key was then completed by reading.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_A.md and reading_B.md, README word rule: letter A 344 words read and 23 holes (0.937), letter B 154 read and 12 holes (0.928), both 498 of 533 = 0.934; holes recounted at integration (A 363 words, B 166). The contributor's unit figures, given once: 2,204 of 2,368 = 93.07% with d and t from the blind shape test, 2,247 = 94.89% with the non-blind second look, 2,161 = 91.26% with the key alone (P printed t); 73 units unread.

gaps.item: d and t: one transcription code (P) for two shapes, 256 units; a blind shape test agrees with the non-blind look on 82.8%
gaps.detail: The shapes are not reliably told apart on the image, so d or t is chosen from context. A person reading the heads on the original, or a blind re-transcription that splits the two shapes, would settle it.

gaps.item: 73 unread units in 16 places: L05, L08, L17 (a name), L21, V03, B12 (a place near Piadena), B16-B17
gaps.detail: holes.md lists them; looked at again on the image on 12 Nov 2026 and left unread.

The l shape (sign D) has no blind confirmation; the second look at d and t was not blind
gaps.detail: The blind classifier put most l signs in the d class.

texts.label: Rossi to Ferrante Gonzaga, San Secondo, 4 Nov 1537, cc. 31r-31v
texts.summary: Written after supper and, the count says, a good deal of wine. He mocks an Imperial commander he calls Astolfo, who had announced all over Italy that he would fight the French and has instead retreated twenty miles, with forty to follow. Cesare Pallavicino has ridden to the Marquis to see the retreat. He recalls a departure from Genoa the December before, and excuses his free speech by the wine and by not having to deal with Covos.

reading_review.by: the integration reader (a Claude model, 12 Nov 2026): a model reading, not a person; it replaces the contributor's own entry and is not independent of the model-assisted work
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the translation. The letter runs as connected, jocular Italian in the writer's north-Italian spelling; the verso is close to clean. The recto has the holes: two unread groups in one sentence (L08), an unread name (L17), an unread phrase (L21), and several words whose letters are read but whose sense is doubtful ('verna fra', 'com a vano', 'tale voche').

texts.note: read_share 0.937 is our count of the README word rule on reading_A.md (344 words read and 23 holes, 367 in all): unread groups, doubtful words and every word with a supplied letter count as holes. By cipher units letter A is 92.19% (blind d/t) to 94.42% (non-blind d/t). transcription_blind.txt is the blind second transcription of both letters, in its own sign names (transcription_blind_signs.tsv).

texts.label: Rossi to Ferrante Gonzaga, San Secondo, 8 Nov 1537, c. 33r
texts.summary: Four days later. The second retreat of 'this coward Astolfo' was forty miles as foretold, with twelve guns lost; Pinerolo and Turin are relieved; there is no money. Men from Mirandola have raided the Cremonese and sacked Piadena and another place. He breaks off to keep company with 'your prince of Luzara', who must be put to bed after supper.

reading_review.by: the integration reader (a Claude model, 12 Nov 2026): a model reading, not a person; it replaces the contributor's own entry and is not independent of the model-assisted work
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the translation. Coherent throughout. Holes: a place-name after 'Castel', the end of the last sentence but one ('non mi lassa ... com[...]gie'), one clause whose words are doubtful ('per le valli meglio la comodita'), and three supplied letters.

texts.note: read_share 0.928 is our count of the README word rule on reading_B.md (154 words read and 12 holes, 166 in all). By cipher units letter B is 94.97% (blind d/t) to 95.89% (non-blind d/t).

outcome.notes: Filed as read in part: 0.934 of the two letters by the README word rule (A 0.937, B 0.928), under the 95% bar; by cipher units 93.07% with d and t from the blind shape test and 94.89% with the non-blind look (the contributor's). The d/t point is the main limit: one code for two shapes, the blind test tells them apart about four times in five, so the reading chooses d or t from context. The statistical test (docs/_validate.py) is 'underdetermined': an annealer started from a random key on the real ciphertext reaches -2.323 per letter against -2.330 for the reading, so the letter model cannot tell the reading from a fitted key; shuffled-key and null controls are the contributor's own. Order of events (first transcription frozen before decoding) is by the contributor's record; the RFC 3161 imprints and stamped files agree with it. The repository's checker scripts were not run by the contributor.
